name: Cyril Ramaphosa
role: President of South Africa (2018–present); ANC president (2017–present)
summary: A former mineworkers' union leader and ANC negotiator who became a businessman before returning to lead the ANC and South Africa. He pursues non-racial democracy, black economic empowerment, universal health insurance and market-opening reform of state utilities, and leads a multiparty coalition government. In foreign policy he stresses multilateralism, UN reform, African peacekeeping and Global South development.

universal-healthcare.rationale: He signed the National Health Insurance Bill into law, creating a fund to give all residents equal access to health care.

unions-good.rationale: He founded and led the National Union of Mineworkers and helped found COSATU, building the union to some 300,000 members.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: He says black South Africans were deliberately excluded and that a R20bn-a-year transformation fund and empowerment of black people are 'righting a grave historical wrong'.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He calls climate change an existential threat and urges faster emission cuts, while saying South Africa will cut emissions at a pace it can afford.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He says government is closing tariff loopholes and developing measures to protect jobs in steel, automotive and manufacturing.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He announces a state industrial policy and tax incentives (150% deduction for new energy vehicles) aimed at chosen industries.

right-to-secede.rationale: Asked about a Western Cape secession referendum, he replied that the Constitution makes South Africa one sovereign democratic state and that he will hold no such referendum.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He says he wants a nation united in its diversity, bringing together people of different races, cultures, languages and ethnic groups.

national-self-determination.rationale: He calls for the Palestinian and Western Saharan peoples' right to self-determination and a Palestinian state beside Israel.

force-without-un.rationale: He criticises unilateral military action in contravention of international law and says the UN must be central.

class-collaboration.rationale: He calls partnerships between government, business and labour models of cooperation and builds policy on them.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He calls apartheid a crime against humanity and states that the country stands for non-racialism.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He states that the country stands for equal rights for women, persons with disability and LGBTQIA+ people, and the Freedom Charter vision that all are equal before the law.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He endorses the Freedom Charter's vision of government founded on the will of the people as the one guiding his government.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: He presents cooperation among people of different backgrounds, races, languages and ethnic groups as the source of national strength.

constituent-assembly.rationale: He chaired the Constitutional Assembly (1994-96), the elected body that drafted the post-apartheid constitution.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He calls on wealthier countries to meet financial commitments and raise climate finance and development support for poorer countries.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: He calls for the Charter ban on annexation of land by force to be applied to Israeli-occupied Palestinian land.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: He sets out race-targeted empowerment (a transformation fund for black-owned enterprises) as government policy because of deliberate exclusion.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He calls the Constitution with its Bill of Rights, adopted by the Constitutional Assembly he chaired, a great moment and the basis of the nation's rights.

public-access-to-information.rationale: He lists the Promotion of Access to Information Act, giving effect to the constitutional right of access to information, among the country's human-rights achievements.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: He says South Africa will not be bullied and will defend its sovereignty and national interest.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The NHI Act he signed has the fund buy services from both public and private providers.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: He says South Africa stands for equal rights for members of the LGBTQIA+ community and for upholding their dignity.

social-market-economy.rationale: He pairs market reforms and private investment with a large social wage (around 60% of the budget) and grants.

racial-franchise.rationale: He describes the vision of a united, non-racial, democratic South Africa as the guide of his government and says the country stands for non-racialism and democracy.

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: He describes South African troops deployed in the DRC and Mozambique as peacekeepers defending others' right to peace.

future-generations.rationale: He says present needs must be met without compromising future generations and that failing to curb warming fails them.

arms-reduction.rationale: He says the world is building weapons when it should build social infrastructure and calls for silencing the guns.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: He calls for reform of international financial institutions, fairer lending rules and redirected Special Drawing Rights to favour developing countries.

women-suffrage.rationale: He reaffirms South Africa's commitment to women's full, equal and meaningful participation in all spheres of life.

recognize-territorial-claims-from-conque.rationale: He says the prohibition on annexing land through the use of force must be upheld and insists on territorial integrity for every country.

notes: Themes searched: economy, society, race, government, world and ecology, in his State of the Nation addresses (2025, 2026), UN General Assembly speeches, Davos 2025, and the acts he signed. No answer rests on his business or Marikana conduct, which is not a stated position. Most statements outside these texts are null. Also searched, with no position that settles the statements: religion and the state (interfaith and schools speeches), devolution and local government (District Development Model), minority languages. Lines 14 and 4 remain too wide.
